subsystems.name: Active molecule
subsystems.role: the compound intended to alter how a gene is read — either by loosening or tightening the packaging around DNA.
parts: NAD+ precursors such as nicotinamide riboside
DNA methyltransferase modulators and methyl donors

subsystems.name: Delivery system
subsystems.role: carries the active across the stratum corneum, the skin's main barrier.

subsystems.name: Target cells
subsystems.role: the cells whose gene expression should actually change.
parts: dermal fibroblasts (produce collagen I and III)

subsystems.name: Assay and biomarker suite
subsystems.role: proves the molecule reached the cell and changed the intended mark, not just that skin felt smoother.
parts: histone acetylation and DNA methylation staining

subsystems.name: Formulation base
subsystems.role: keeps a chemically fragile active stable on the shelf.

subsystems.name: Safety assessment
subsystems.role: checks the active is not switching genes in the wrong tissue.
parts: skin absorption and systemic exposure measurements

buildSteps.title: Choose a target mark
buildSteps.detail: Map what actually changes with age in skin — for example reduced histone acetylation or altered DNA methylation at the collagen gene promoter — and pick one to reverse.

buildSteps.title: Screen candidate molecules
buildSteps.detail: Test libraries of HDAC inhibitors, sirtuin activators and NAD+ precursors on cultured fibroblasts and on lab-grown human skin equivalents, measuring collagen messenger RNA and protein.

buildSteps.title: Test penetration
buildSteps.detail: Apply the candidate to human skin explants in diffusion cells and measure how much active crosses into the dermis. Most molecules above roughly 500 daltons, or water-soluble ones, barely pass.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the active in lipid vesicles or load it into dissolving microneedles so enough reaches the fibroblasts without irritating the surface.

buildSteps.title: Confirm target engagement
buildSteps.detail: Run biopsies rather than cosmetic swabs: check the specific histone or methylation mark changed in the intended cells, not merely that a cream was applied.

buildSteps.title: Check selectivity and safety
buildSteps.detail: HDAC inhibitors are also approved systemic cancer drugs, so off-target effects in other tissues and any cancer-promoting risk must be excluded before long-term human use.

buildSteps.title: Run controlled human trials
buildSteps.detail: Randomised trials with biopsy endpoints at 12–24 weeks, comparing against a vehicle control, to separate the active from the moisturising base.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacture
buildSteps.detail: Fix the molecule and its formulation, then move to good-manufacturing-practice production with stability testing at 25 °C and 40 °C.

prerequisites.tech: Topical delivery of molecules into the dermis
prerequisites.why: microneedles and vesicle systems work in principle, but reproducible delivery of a defined dose of a small-molecule modulator is not routine.

prerequisites.tech: Validated epigenetic markers of skin ageing
prerequisites.why: age-related methylation and acetylation changes are documented in skin, but no single mark is confirmed as a reliable lever for collagen output.

prerequisites.tech: Selective, long-term-safe HDAC and sirtuin modulators
prerequisites.why: existing HDAC inhibitor drugs are potent systemic agents; a version safe for daily cosmetic use on healthy skin does not exist.

prerequisites.tech: Human skin models and biopsy-based assays
prerequisites.why: skin equivalents, explant cultures and chromatin assays are standard laboratory tools, so the testing route is open.
retinoids already demonstrate that topical agents can raise collagen production via nuclear receptors, giving a validated benchmark.

pathway.milestone: marketed 'epigenetic' serums built on NAD+ precursors and sirtuin-activating plant extracts
pathway.unlocks: consumer familiarity, but public evidence for biopsy-confirmed changes in human skin is essentially absent.

pathway.milestone: topical actives with published target-engagement data — a measured change in a specific epigenetic mark in human skin
pathway.unlocks: turning a marketing category into a measurable mechanism.

pathway.milestone: delivery breakthroughs letting larger, more selective modulators reach fibroblasts at controlled doses
pathway.unlocks: real dose–response data instead of in-vitro-only results.

pathway.milestone: controlled trials with collagen endpoints, regulated as drugs rather than cosmetics
pathway.unlocks: a defensible claim to modify skin ageing at the level of gene expression, possibly combined with senolytic or partial-reprogramming research.
